original_card.question: Can an explicitly larger or nonabelian register model escape the scoped three-register obstruction?
methods: Construct the smallest exact identity in a newly specified legal operation alphabet.
Derive a target-specific relaxation bound for that same explicit alphabet.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Name the changed hypothesis, all counted roles and a uniform identity; finite column tests alone do not certify it.

first_step.inspect: Read Model section 1 of the three-register bound and identify the exact excluded free operations.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Write a complete operation alphabet outside one named premise and price a baseline before searching identities.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A small-width completed saving changes the bit primitive; a finite-address identity alone is insufficient.
allowed_variations: Choose a fixed larger register count or a specified nonabelian operation family.
scope_change_triggers: Remaining inside the already-excluded three-register abelian model.

actual_scope: Exact minimum of six paid coordinate-CNOT address calls for two coordinate-SWAP targets in M_r(F2[GL_2(F2)]), for every finite r>=2 with arbitrary restored dirty registers and free scalar GL_r(F2) mixing.
scope_change_reason: The card permits a specified nonabelian operation family. PR1333 already settles the broader rank-priced affine model; its first open next question restricts paid labels to coordinate CNOTs. This takes the smallest two-target gap instance and strengthens the initial r=2,3 census to a written all-register proof on that same target.
bottleneck_link: Scoped no-gain side result for a changed address model: in this smallest restricted-alphabet gap, extra dirty registers cannot reduce the direct paid-call bill. This is not a selected supplier or kappa improvement.
stop_rule: Stop when the exact two-SWAP target is resolved or after one bounded pivot; at most 60 minutes with final quarter for validation. No broader register-model search.
evidence: PROOF.md gives the all-register sign-trace and coefficient-rank argument. EXPECTED.json binds exact r=2,3 formal/dense state-set equality, empty radius-2/radius-3 intersections, a six-call witness, 31 symbolic patterns, 4704 scalar conjugations and 14 boundary controls.
author: commdata2338
ai_assistance: Prepared for commdata2338 (@commdata2338), with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. No subagents or independent human review.

open_questions.question: Can three or more coordinate-SWAP targets share paid calls in this same two-label formal model?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The current obstruction closes exactly two targets; it does not prove a general 3w direct-sum law.
open_questions.first_step: For w=3, use the sign-trace parity s=1 mod2 and seek a coefficient-rank obstruction or an exact formal word with at most seven calls, versus the direct nine.
open_questions.blocked_by: The four-call coefficient proof does not cover longer alternating patterns; arbitrary dirty-register counts require a new argument.

open_questions.question: Does a genuinely three-dimensional coordinate-CNOT target with a rank-versus-word-length gap permit savings across two roles?
open_questions.why_it_matters: This is the higher-dimensional branch of PR1333 first open question, outside the two-dimensional target settled here.
open_questions.first_step: Choose a fixed GL_3(F2) target with certified coordinate-CNOT length above rank(A-I); pin its complete alphabet and compare exact two-role formal words to twice the direct length.
open_questions.blocked_by: Need a new sign/rank functional or a bounded exact search with full group-algebra equality and complete paid/restoration bill.

chooser.selected_method: Derive a target-specific relaxation bound for that same explicit alphabet.
